So — notes and snippets below. Keeping this tight so we can include directly in Acme's checklist.

Network and ports (on-prem VPC model):
- Splunk HEC: TCP 443 (HEC token auth over TLS). Endpoint example: https://hec-collector.acme.internal:443/services/collector/event
- Syslog over TLS (RFC5425): TCP 6514 (server-side cert required).
- OTLP/HTTP (OTLP over gRPC optional): TCP 4318 for OTLP/HTTP, TCP 4317 for OTLP/gRPC. Jaeger thrift (legacy) commonly uses 14268 (HTTP).
- Prometheus scrape: your Prometheus should be able to reach service endpoints on port 9100/metrics (service-level). We typically expose metrics on 9100 with a path /metrics.

Certificate & rotation guidance:
- We support mTLS and TLS. For Splunk HEC, token-based auth is primary; if you require mutual TLS we can supply CA pinning guidance.
- Recommend cert rotation every 90 days for edge forwarders; internal service certs can follow your standard cadence.

Sample rsyslog snippet (forward to Splunk HEC-compatible syslog receiver):
# /etc/rsyslog.d/50-redwood.conf
module(load="imfile")
input(type="imfile" File="/var/log/redwood/app.log" Tag="redwood-app" Severity="info")
action(type="omfwd" Protocol="tcp" Target="splunk-syslog.acme.internal" Port="6514" StreamDriver="gtls" StreamDriverMode="1" ActionResumeRetryCount="-1")

Notes on batching & backpressure:
- Forwarders buffer to disk and batch at ~1-5s by default; increase batch size for high-volume customers.
- Include high-water metrics to your monitoring so we can surface forwarding backpressure.

Attachments: rsyslog_example.conf (small stub).

-Karthik
